data.name: Akshaya
data.gender_notes: Akshaya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Akshaya is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘अक्षय’, which means ‘infinite’, ‘inexhaustible’, ‘unending’, or ‘perpetual’. This name is often used to denote something that never diminishes or decreases. In Hindu mythology, Lord Vishnu is also known by the name Akshaya, which signifies his infinite power and presence. The name Akshaya carries the meaning “Infinite, Inexhaustible” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Akshaya usually hope their child will grow to embody infinite, inexhaustible and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of eternal life and divine grace.
data.etymology: Akshaya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Infinite, Inexhaustible.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Akshaya total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

The name is associated with joy, prosperity, and good fortune, which are essential elements of Hindu culture. Akshaya is a name used to celebrate the virtues of perseverance, affirmation of life, and a hopeful outlook towards the future.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Akshaya signifies the inherent divinity within each individual, representing the unchanging and infinite essence of the soul. It is a reminder that no matter what challenges we face in life, the spirit inside us remains unaltered and eternal. Additionally, the name Akshaya is a call to cultivate this inner divine quality in our everyday lives, leading us towards a state of spiritual fulfillment and self-realization.
